extra.message: Insecure deserialization (pickle.loads) of request body — Remote code execution on the server (full host compromise) by sending a crafted pickle payload. [verified: Line 61 pickle.loads() on raw request body/base64 blob with no type restriction yields RCE via __reduce__; only the static shared INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN header gates it, which is authentication, not deserialization safety.]

Path traversal arbitrary file write and plaintext PII storage — Arbitrary file write outside the export directory and plaintext sensitive data (SSN/PAN) at rest. [verified: Line 70-71 builds BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f'{ref}.json' from user-controlled 'ref' without sanitizing separators (traversal write) and write_text()s SSN/card PII in plaintext.]

Code injection via eval() of user expression — Arbitrary expression/code execution leading to potential RCE or sandbox escape. [verified: Line 84 eval(expr,...) on the user 'expr' query param; emptying __builtins__ is not a sandbox since dunder/attribute chains remain reachable, making this exploitable code injection.]

CORS origin reflection with credentials — Any malicious origin can make credentialed cross-origin requests and read responses. [verified: Lines 132-134 reflect the request Origin into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and set Access-Control-Allow-Credentials:true, letting any origin make credentialed cross-origin reads (the global CORSMiddleware allowlist is bypassed by these manually-set response headers).]

Server-side template injection (Jinja2 render of user input) — Server-side template injection enabling arbitrary code execution / data exfiltration. [verified: Line 152 renders Template('Result: '+fragment) where fragment is the raw user query param, so {{7*7}}/{{cycler...}} payloads execute server-side—classic SSTI to RCE.]

Arbitrary file write via path traversal in filename — Arbitrary file write (e.g. overwrite code/config) potentially leading to RCE. [verified: Line 159 writes raw body to BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name where 'name' is an unsanitized user query param, so '../' sequences enable arbitrary file write outside the export dir.]

XXE via lxml parser with external entities enabled — Local file disclosure and SSRF via XML external entity expansion. [verified: Line 191 builds etree.XMLParser(load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False) and parses the raw body, enabling file:// disclosure and SSRF via external entities.]

NoSQL/Mongo query injection from request body — Unauthorized read of arbitrary MongoDB documents via attacker-controlled query operators. [verified: Line 188 passes attacker-controlled payload['filter'] (or whole JSON body) directly to MongoClient...find_one(query), allowing operator injection ($ne/$gt/$where) to read arbitrary documents.]

Password reset token written in cleartext to log file — Account takeover: reading the log yields valid reset tokens to set arbitrary user passwords. [verified: request_password_reset writes the cleartext reset token `raw` plus the user email to password_reset_tokens.log (auth.py:215-220) with no dev/env guard, defeating the hashed-at-rest design; file-read access yields valid tokens enabling account takeover via /password-reset/confirm.]

Sensitive data (Authorization header/body) written to logs — Credential/secret disclosure to log files and log forging/injection. [verified: Line 33 logger.warning logs the full request body and the verbatim Authorization header, leaking bearer/secret credentials to logs and permitting CRLF log injection.]

Open redirect via user-controlled redirect target — Phishing/credential harvesting by redirecting users to attacker-controlled URLs. [verified: Line 39 returns RedirectResponse(lane) with 'lane' a fully user-controlled query param and no allowlist/relative enforcement, enabling open redirect to external sites.]

Reflected XSS via |safe in HTML response — Reflected cross-site scripting in browser context (script execution, session/credential theft). [verified: Lines 121-122 render Template('{{ card|safe }}') with the user 'card' param and return it via HTMLResponse; |safe disables autoescaping so attacker HTML/JS is reflected unescaped.]

Missing brute-force/rate-limit protection on login — Credential brute-forcing / password guessing against any account. [verified: The /api/auth/login handler runs unbounded bcrypt verify_password attempts and no rate-limiting/lockout library or middleware exists anywhere (only CORS and SecurityHeaders middleware in main.py), so credential brute-forcing is unthrottled.]

Verbose error exposing internal details — Disclosure of internal filesystem paths and implementation details aiding further attacks. [verified: Line 26 returns str(exc) and exc.__class__.__name__ to the client, leaking BASE_EXPORT_DIR path and implementation details in a verbose error.]

Security headers disabled (empty CSP, XSS protection off) — Removes browser-side XSS/clickjacking mitigations for the response. [verified: Lines 175-176 set X-XSS-Protection:0 and an empty Content-Security-Policy which override the SecurityHeadersMiddleware setdefault defaults, disabling XSS/framing mitigations for this response.]
